title: Fallback tier + spot sensitivity analysis
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a working draft for the spreadsheet-backed sensitivity analysis used to recommend default smart-routing policies for Hosted API and Dedicated customers. Focus is on how fallback tiers (hot / warm / cold), cross-region routing, and spot vs on-demand capacity interact to drive unit cost and SLA risk.

High-level goals (what we want from the model):
- Produce a per-request expected-cost distribution under configurable workload profiles (p50/p90/p99 tokens per request, request arrival process).
- Capture spot preemption risk and expected preemption cost (retry + failover latency + extra token cost).
- Provide simple policy knobs that map to cost delta vs expected latency increase (e.g., allow-spot=true, max-regional-hop=1, fallback-tier-stepdown=warm->cold).
- Surface failure modes where cost savings are not worth SLA degradation.

Spreadsheet structure (tabs in the working XLS):
- inputs: workload profile, token-length distribution, arrival lambda, SLA targets (p99 latency, error budget), region costs (spot/on-demand base prices + observed preemption rate), inter-region latency penalty matrix
- cost-model: per-route expected token cost, request-level amortized overheads, preemption expected extra cost line items
- routing-policy-sim: policy definitions (priority list, tier caps, spot-allowed flag, max-hops) and simulated outcomes over N=100k random requests
- sensitivity: sweep spot price, preemption rate, inter-region bandwidth latency, and capacity headroom. Outputs: cost delta, p99 latency delta, error-rate delta, percent of requests failing SLA
- heuristics: recommended policy mappings by customer tier (startup, scale, enterprise) and short rationale

Key model assumptions (explicit)
- Spot price = baseline GPU-hour * spot-discount. We model spot preemption as an exponential process with lambda_prep; preemption probability for a request roughly = 1 - exp(-lambda_prep * request_duration_hours).
- Request_duration_hours approximated from tokens -> tokens_per_second (default 20 t/s) -> seconds -> hours.
- Failover cost = token-waste (tokens generated on preempted run) + requeue overhead (average 200ms) + fallback-model-latency-increase (per-policy configured). For heavy workloads we include partial KV-cache loss penalty when fallback model is a different family.
- Inter-region routing imposes latency penalty L(regionA->regionB) read from latency matrix; we add both network RTT and cold-start penalty when routing to a cold region where no warm pool exists.

Representative baseline numbers used for initial sweeps (editable on inputs tab)
- on-demand g4x: $4.50 / GPU-hour (example)
- spot discount: 65% -> spot = $1.58 / GPU-hour
- observed preemption rate (lambda_prep baseline): 0.03 per hour (i.e., 3%/hr)
- avg tokens per request: p50=350, p90=1200, p99=2200
- tokens/sec throughput per GPU (serving flavor): 50 t/s for small models, 22 t/s for large models
- cost per token simplified = (GPU-hour price)/(3600 * throughput t/s) -> gives baseline per-token.

Sensitivity experiments run so far (summary):
1) Vary spot preemption rate 0.01-0.12/hr, keep spot price constant. Findings: cost savings from spot flatten after lambda_prep > 0.07/hr because retry + duplicate token cost dominate. For p90/p99 heavy workloads, spot use should be limited to non-latency-critical tiers (cold/warm only) unless warm-cache can be restored cheaply.
2) Vary spot discount 40%-80% at fixed preemption. If discount <50% savings on p99 workloads becomes marginal unless capacity headroom is large (>20%).
3) Cross-region penalty sweep: adding 40ms one-way to reach alternate region increases p99 by ~150-250ms for typical request shapes (because tails amplify). Cost delta sometimes positive (cheaper compute in remote region) but SLA failures spike.

Practical routing policy recommendations (draft):
- Default policy (startup / free-tier): allow-spot=true but only in cold tier; max-hops=0 (no cross-region), fallback-policy: warm->cold with aggressive cache warming (pre-warm on detected demand). Rationale: maximize cost savings while containing latency risks for low-SLA workloads.
- Scale (SMB) policy: allow-spot=true in warm-tier up to 20% capacity; reserve on-demand for hot-tier. Max-hops=1 allowed to nearest cheaper region if p99 impact < 10% of SLA. Use short warm-cache TTL (90s) to reduce preemption cost.
- Enterprise policy: allow-spot=false by default for hot and warm; cold can use spot for background batch work. Cross-region allowed only for overflow with explicit rollback thresholds. Enterprise customers can opt into aggressive spot saves via config flags with SLA exceptions and audit logs.

Example policy encoding (human-readable rules used by planner):
- policy.v1 {
    hot_pool: [region-local, on_demand_only],
    warm_pool: [region-local, allow_spot: false for enterprise, true for scale/startup],
    cold_pool: [cross_region_allowed: true, prefer_spot: true],
    fallback_order: hot -> warm -> cold,
    max_cross_region_hops: 1,
    spot_capacity_cap_pct: 20
  }
(we store these as rows in routing-policy spreadsheet with params serialized as strings for the rules engine to parse)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to model partial KV cache reuse cost when fallback model is same family but different quantization (empirically measured soft penalty vs full cold start)? Need perf traces (linked ticket JIRA-OPT-462).
- Should we include bandwidth egress cost when cross-region routing is used heavily? Currently we omit egress pricing; it matters for large-context models with streaming.
- Simpler user config UX: map knobs to 3 sliders (cost priority / latency priority / availability priority) and convert to precise policy. Need design input from console team (Sofia).
- Validate preemption model against 3 months of spot eviction logs (SRE dataset). I requested access (CONFLUENCE-1234).

Quick checklist before propose final defaults:
- [ ] Run sensitivity with real customer workload traces for top 10 Hosted tenants (requesting traces from privacy-safe bucket).
- [ ] Add egress cost in cross-region scenarios and re-run enterprise impact.
- [ ] Coordinate with serving-runtime to quantify caching reheat times for model families A/B/C.
- [ ] Draft simplest UX mapping for product console and get early ops feedback.

Notes to self (scratch):
- If spot preemption cost model includes probability-weighted token-waste, the marginal savings is approx: savings = (on_demand_cost - spot_cost) * (1 - prob(preempt)*retry_penalty_factor) - prob(preempt)*extra_latency_cost
- For high-tail workloads, target to keep >75% of p99 requests on on-demand in hot/warm. Must communicate to sales: "20% spot cap on warm gives ~28% cost reduction in steady state for model X under baseline traffic" (example number from spreadsheet tab).

Appendix: spreadsheet columns called out explicitly (for reviewer to check tabs)
- inputs: workload_name, p50_tokens, p90_tokens, p99_tokens, arrival_lambda_per_sec, tokens_per_sec, sld_target_p99_ms, on_demand_price_per_hour, spot_price_per_hour, spot_lambda_prep_per_hour, region_latency_penalty_ms
- sim rows: request_id, arrival_ts, tokens, chosen_policy, chosen_region, chosen_tier, preempted(boolean), preemption_time, tokens_wasted, rerun_latency_ms, final_latency_ms, cost_immediate, cost_total

If anything here is unclear ping me in #product-optimize or drop comment on JIRA-OPT-462.

Working files: fallback_sensitivity_v3.xlsx (tabbed), sim_runs/seed-20260301.csv (seeded Monte Carlo), notes: routing-policy-ux-v1.sketch (draft).

End.
